claims.text: Phonon-mediated superconductivity governs superconducting behavior in high-entropy alloys.
The presence of multiple principal elements alters phonon dispersion.
The presence of multiple principal elements alters electron-phonon coupling.
Altered phonon dispersion and electron-phonon coupling enhance the superconducting critical temperature.
CoCrFeMnNi is an FCC solid solution under the proposed conditions.
The specified CoCrFeMnNi alloy is in a superconducting state.
Neutron scattering can be used to probe phonon dispersion in the proposed alloy.
Scanning tunneling spectroscopy can be used to probe electron-phonon coupling in the proposed alloy.
The comparison will be performed at 4.2 K and pressures from 0 to 10 GPa.
The CoCrFeMnNi alloy is predicted to have a critical temperature of 12 K at 0 GPa.
The CoCrFeMnNi alloy is predicted to have a critical temperature of 15 K at 10 GPa.
The high-entropy alloy is predicted to have a superconducting critical temperature 20% higher than traditional alloys.
Ni or Co can serve as single-principal-element traditional-alloy baselines.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to FCC CoCrFeMnNi under low-temperature conditions and pressures no higher than 10 GPa.
A controlled comparison will measure critical temperature, phonon dispersion, and electron-phonon coupling in the high-entropy alloy and traditional-alloy baseline.
The hypothesis will be falsified if the high-entropy alloy's critical temperature at 0 GPa is less than 15% higher than the traditional-alloy baseline.
The hypothesis will be falsified if phonon dispersion and electron-phonon coupling are not significantly altered relative to traditional alloys.
